decision_table.name: Determine_KS_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Kansas state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in KS (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
KS filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in KS if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in KS - Employees working in KS - Tangible personal property located in KS - Real property located in KS
Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,138 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: Kansas Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Booklet 2025

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
KS filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions in KS.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), KS requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus thresholds, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Kansas Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance

No KS nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,138 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_KS_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate KS state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
KS state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
KS ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to KS) - State income tax refunds included in federal taxable income - Business interest expense carryforward deductions under IRC Section 163(j) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Expenses related to exempt income
KS SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on Kansas state and municipal bonds - Kansas net operating loss deduction (subject to KS limitations) - State income taxes paid during the taxable year - Certain refunds of state income taxes
Reference: Kansas Form K-120 Schedule S (Additions and Subtractions) Reference: Kansas Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Booklet 2025 Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,117 (Adjustments to federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have KS nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_KS_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate KS state corporate income tax. Applies KS two-tier rate structure: 4.0% base + 3.0% surtax on income over $50,000.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
KS state corporate income tax calculation with surtax:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to KS: × [KS apportionment percentage] 3. KS additions: + [Federal interest, state tax refunds, IRC 163(j), etc.] 4. KS subtractions: - [KS municipal interest, KS NOL, state taxes paid, etc.] 5. KS taxable income: = [Result]
Two-tier tax calculation: 6a. Base tax on ALL income: [Taxable income] × 4.0% 6b. Surtax on income over $50,000: [Amount over $50,000] × 3.0% 7. Total KS tax before credits: = [Base tax + Surtax]
8. KS credits: - [Job creation, film, historic preservation, etc.] 9. KS tax liability: = [Final tax]
Example calculation for $150,000 taxable income: - Base tax: $150,000 × 4.0% = $6,000 - Surtax: ($150,000 - $50,000) × 3.0% = $3,000 - Total tax: $6,000 + $3,000 = $9,000 - Effective rate: $9,000 / $150,000 = 6.0%
KS apportionment formula: - Current (2025-2026): Three-factor (property, payroll, sales) - Optional: Two-factor (sales and property) if payroll exceeds 200% average - Future (2027+): Single-sales factor per House Bill 2231
KS provides various tax credits including: - Job creation and expansion credits - Film production credits - Historic preservation credits - Community service contribution credits - Research and development credits
Reference: Kansas Form K-120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,110 (Tax rate: 4.0% + 3.0% surtax over $50,000) Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,138 (Three-factor apportionment) Reference: Kansas Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Booklet 2025 Reference: House Bill 2231 (2025) - Single sales factor for 2027+

KS state corporate income tax calculation without surtax.
Income does not exceed $50,000 surtax threshold, so only base rate applies.
Tax calculation: 1. KS taxable income: [Amount $50,000 or less] 2. Base tax: [Taxable income] × 4.0% 3. Surtax: $0 (threshold not exceeded) 4. Total tax before credits: = [Base tax] 5. KS credits: - [Job creation, film, historic preservation, etc.] 6. KS tax liability: = [Final tax]
Example calculation for $30,000 taxable income: - Base tax: $30,000 × 4.0% = $1,200 - Surtax: $0 (below $50,000 threshold) - Total tax: $1,200 - Effective rate: $1,200 / $30,000 = 4.0%
Reference: Kansas Form K-120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,110 (Tax rate: 4.0% base rate) Reference: Kansas Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Booklet 2025

No KS nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in KS. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,138 (Nexus requirements)

No KS taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has KS nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
KS net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - KS allows NOL carryforward - NOL limited to percentage of taxable income (similar to federal)
Reference: Kansas Form K-120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: K.S.A. 79-32,143 (Net operating loss deduction) Reference: Kansas Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Booklet 2025
